newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bonds higher across the board.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed higher across the board on Tuesday while unlinked bonds traded stable awaiting publication of July's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.16 pct to 111.3
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.18 pct to 111.59
* Unlinked government bonds: unchanged at 110.23
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.36 pct to 111.35
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 108.49
Volume including Makams was an average 178 million shekels.

"Prices of all CPI-linked bonds rose today in active trading," said Ofer Agassi of the Financial Immunities consulting firm. "Yields on these bonds are continuing to fall and will continue to do so," he said.
Agassi said the falling yields were due to a tight supply of CPI-linked bonds.

Government bond redemptions are expected to total four billion shekels in August against issues of 1.4-1.6 billion shekels; a successful privatisation process and higher tax revenues are all expected to lessen the government's need to raise debt on the bond market.
Traders said that the shortage was expected to affect all government bonds, but especially CPI-linked bonds.
"The government is not issuing any new CPI-linked bonds, only unlinked bonds" said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment.
Prices of unlinked bonds were stable on Tuesday, Alt said. "Traders are waiting for July's CPI to be published," he said.
The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices in July and August.
July's CPI will be published on August 15.
Yields of one-year unlinked bonds were around 13 percent, Alt said.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds closed higher on Tuesday on the rise of the dollar against the shekel, Agassi said.
The shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly lower against the dollar on Tuesday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5440 shekels compared with 3.5410 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.54 shekels)
